symbols.label: readInt
symbols.detail: Read an integer from standard input.
symbols.documentation: Runtime input helper. The editor can add either the stoud facade import or the legacy runtime import; ncc remains authoritative.

symbols.label: readLine
symbols.detail: Read a text line from standard input.
symbols.documentation: Standard safe input surface.

symbols.label: readBool
symbols.detail: Read a boolean value from standard input.
symbols.documentation: Standard safe input surface.

symbols.label: print
symbols.detail: Write human output without adding a newline.
symbols.documentation: Standard output surface. For strict profiles prefer explicit render helpers when printing non-text values.

symbols.label: println
symbols.documentation: Standard output surface.

symbols.label: color
symbols.detail: Render text with an ANSI foreground color.
symbols.documentation: color returns a printable string decorated with the selected terminal color when the runtime output channel supports ANSI. Use it inside print or println for compact, readable terminal UI.

symbols.label: colorBold
symbols.detail: Render text with bold ANSI color.
symbols.documentation: colorBold is the normal helper for menu headings, status banners and highlighted output. It shares the output family with print and println, while render keeps numeric conversion explicit.

symbols.label: \n
symbols.documentation: Inside a string literal, \n is decoded by the lexer as a real newline before the output runtime receives the text.

symbols.detail: Literal ampersand escape inside print strings.
symbols.documentation: \& prints a literal ampersand. It exists so future symbolic print controls can remain explicit without making normal text awkward.

symbols.detail: Literal question-mark escape inside print strings.
symbols.documentation: \? prints a literal question mark and gives menu prompts a stable escape for contexts where question marks may later become print controls.

symbols.detail: Literal hash escape inside print strings.
symbols.documentation: \# prints a literal hash. Use it when text should not be interpreted as a print-family control marker.

symbols.detail: Separator marker for print and println.
symbols.documentation: When the complete payload is ##, the output runtime expands it to a stable separator line for menus, reports and CLI sections.

symbols.label: renderInt
symbols.detail: Render an integer explicitly for text output.
symbols.documentation: Explicit render helper used by strict text/plus diagnostics.

symbols.label: renderBool
symbols.detail: Render a boolean explicitly for text output.
symbols.documentation: Explicit render helper.

symbols.label: renderBinary
symbols.detail: Render an integer as exact binary text.
symbols.documentation: Explicit binary render helper for integer output. The runtime may use an OS-backed %b provider when available and falls back to exact portable bytes.

symbols.label: renderBin
symbols.documentation: Short binary render helper. It follows the same output contract as renderBinary.

symbols.label: strLen
symbols.detail: Count logical characters in a string.
symbols.documentation: Returns the logical character length used by the runtime executor. Use strByteLen when byte size matters for backend buffers or native interop.

symbols.label: strByteLen
symbols.detail: Count UTF-8 bytes in a string.
symbols.documentation: Returns the byte length of the UTF-8 payload. LLVM lowers this through strlen and native-fast emits a byte scan.

symbols.label: strConcat
symbols.documentation: Builds a new string from left plus right. Plain str + str remains valid compact syntax.

symbols.label: strSubstring
symbols.signature: strSubstring(text: str, start: int, len: int) -> str
symbols.detail: Extract a substring by start and length.
symbols.documentation: Returns a string window. Out-of-range runtime execution reports E_RUNTIME_STRING_BOUNDS_001.

symbols.label: strCompare
symbols.documentation: Returns -1 when left sorts before right, 0 when equal, and 1 when left sorts after right.

symbols.label: strContains
symbols.documentation: Returns true when needle appears inside text. For index access use strIndexOf.

symbols.label: strIndexOf
symbols.documentation: Returns the first logical index of needle, or -1 when it is not present.

symbols.label: strFromInt
symbols.documentation: Converts an integer value into text without relying on implicit formatting.

symbols.label: strFromBool
symbols.documentation: Converts true and false to their printable lowercase text forms.

symbols.label: strFromFt64
symbols.documentation: Converts a floating-point value into text for explicit output and concatenation.

symbols.label: renderHex
symbols.detail: Render a number or address as hexadecimal text.
symbols.documentation: Useful for pointer/address reporting.

symbols.label: alloc
symbols.documentation: Allocates count elements and returns p<T>. Storage may be uninitialized. No bounds, ownership or lifetime checks are added in raw mode.

symbols.label: free
symbols.documentation: Releases the address carried by pointer. Existing aliases are unchanged and may dangle; later use or repeated free remains the program's responsibility.

symbols.label: realloc
symbols.documentation: Resizes pointer storage and returns the resulting p<T>. The address may move and old aliases may dangle.

symbols.label: pRegion
symbols.detail: Build a region descriptor from a pointer.
symbols.documentation: Creates memRegion<T> from a raw pointer and explicit length. Raw mode does not prove the address or enforce the declared range.

symbols.label: regionCreate
symbols.detail: Create a runtime memory region with explicit element type and bounds.
symbols.documentation: Region creation helper.

symbols.label: listAsRegion
symbols.detail: Expose a list as a bounded memRegion<T> view.
symbols.documentation: Collection-to-region bridge with explicit bounds.

symbols.label: pFromAddr
symbols.detail: Construct a pointer from an address.
symbols.documentation: Converts a machine address to p<T> without establishing validity, lifetime or alignment.

symbols.label: pCast
symbols.documentation: Changes the pointee type carried by a pointer. No data is moved and no alignment or alias check is inserted.

symbols.label: pNull
symbols.documentation: Returns whether the raw pointer address is zero. It does not validate non-null addresses.

symbols.label: pAddr
symbols.documentation: Returns the machine address carried by p<T>.

symbols.label: pRead
symbols.documentation: Loads T from pointer. Invalid, unaligned, dangling and out-of-range addresses remain permitted raw operations with target-defined consequences.

symbols.label: pWrite
symbols.documentation: Stores T through pointer without implicit bounds, lifetime, ownership or alias checks.

symbols.label: pOffset
symbols.documentation: Computes pointer plus element offset using sizeof(T). Overflow and out-of-range results are not hidden or repaired.

symbols.label: pDiff
symbols.documentation: Returns the element distance between two pointer addresses. The programmer controls provenance and compatibility.

symbols.label: pAt
symbols.detail: Compute a pointer inside a region.
symbols.documentation: Computes base plus index times sizeof(T). Raw mode permits an index outside the declared region.

symbols.label: addrOf
symbols.documentation: Returns the raw machine address of a value or storage location.

symbols.label: spanOf
symbols.documentation: Span retains length/provenance for diagnostics.

symbols.label: sliceOf
symbols.signature: sliceOf<T>(region: memRegion<T>, start: int, len: int) -> slice<T>
symbols.documentation: Slice carries explicit bounds.

symbols.label: parse
symbols.documentation: Specialized compiler-domain surface. It does not grant machine/kernel authority.

symbols.label: fs
symbols.documentation: Requires explicit policy/capability in authorized modes.

symbols.label: runtime
symbols.documentation: Defines a runtime provider container whose exported operations are materialized through the runtime ABI and selected target backend.

symbols.label: compiler
symbols.documentation: Defines compiler-facing code for parsing, semantic analysis, diagnostics, lowering or backend orchestration.

symbols.label: basal
symbols.documentation: Defines the basal root layer used for material identities, bindings, evidence and lower-level continuity.

symbols.label: machine
symbols.documentation: Defines typed machine operations, registers, sections, relocations and ABI-visible instructions.

symbols.label: primitive
symbols.documentation: Defines physical hardware primitives such as buses, ports, signals, MMIO and device contracts.

symbols.label: kernel
symbols.documentation: Defines a freestanding kernel container. Hosted runtime, hidden allocation and implicit dispatch are forbidden.

symbols.label: system
symbols.documentation: Defines a privileged system container. Hardware access, memory effects and ABI boundaries remain explicit and target-dependent.

symbols.label: inspect
symbols.documentation: Defines inspection, tracing and evidence operations whose storage and runtime effects remain explicit.

+ performs numeric addition when operands are numeric. Text composition must remain explicit in strict profiles through render helpers or approved string forms. The IDE explains the operator, but ncc decides overloads, precedence, and diagnostics.

- subtracts numeric values or negates a numeric expression depending on position. Signedness, overflow, and fixed-width behavior are not guessed by the editor. ncc owns the final type, range, and lowering diagnostics.

* multiplies numeric values under the active type contract. For pointer-like code it must not silently become C-style dereference. nC keeps dereference, memory access, and raw hazards explicit so machine lowering and diagnostics remain auditable.

/ divides numeric values. Division by zero, integer truncation, and profile-specific numeric behavior are compiler concerns. The IDE documents the token and precedence, while ncc preserves the actual semantic authority and diagnostics.

% computes remainder for numeric operands. It follows the numeric type contract selected by ncc, including signedness and width. It is not an implicit formatting or pattern token in ordinary expression context.

& combines integer or width-bearing values bit by bit. It is useful for masks, flags, raw memory values, and machine-adjacent code. It must not be confused with implicit address-of; nC keeps address authority explicit through @/addr helpers.

| combines bit fields or flags by setting bits present in either operand. It is width-sensitive and should preserve fixed-size reasoning for byte, word, dword, qword, and signed variants. ncc decides legality and result type.

^ combines bit fields by setting bits that differ. It is common in masks, checksums, encoders, and low-level examples. The operator is fixed-width aware; ncc owns overflow, signedness, and mode-specific validity.

~ flips bits in a width-bearing value. It only makes sense when the width is known or inferred by a valid context. The IDE flags the concept, while ncc diagnoses ambiguous width, signedness, or invalid operand types.

symbols.detail: Projection or shift depending on context.
symbols.documentation: >> is contextual in nC. In declarations such as x >> int <- value it projects a typed binding. In expressions it may represent shift behavior when allowed. Context, type, and mode decide; silent ambiguity is not acceptable.

>>> is the logical right shift spelling used when bits move right and zero-fill behavior matters. It is especially relevant for unsigned and fixed-width values. Arithmetic shift behavior belongs to signed forms and must be documented by type.

-> declares function, routine, or callable return shape depending on mode and surface. It connects parameters to result type rather than performing runtime flow. ncc validates whether the target form is legal for fn, routine, closure, or mode-specific syntax.
Selects a previously declared callable as the program entry. Example: ref main ->> run; does not make run special until this relation exists.

: separates names, type annotations, field contracts, section values, and projection payloads. Its meaning is determined by surrounding grammar. The editor explains the separator, while ncc decides whether a declaration, field, or expression is valid.

:: joins a declared name to its kind, as in run :: fn, and qualifies names where the grammar permits it. Imports use the compact form use <io:output>. Unknown declarations or namespaces are diagnosed.
@ introduces explicit execution domains such as @machine, @runtime, @system, @kernel or @security. Ordinary values and references do not carry this prefix in canonical source.

!> marks verification or assertion-like flow in nC examples. It is intentionally visible because failing checks are semantic evidence, not hidden comments. The IDE explains the token; ncc owns the real diagnostic and execution behavior.

symbols.label: x >> int <- value
symbols.documentation: Declares a place with a physical type and writes its initial bits. Without <- and a value, the place remains uninitialized.
Writes value into a declared or existing place. It performs no allocation, bounds check, ownership transfer or cleanup.

symbols.label: mem[site]
symbols.documentation: mem[site] accesses memory through a named site or region whose provenance is known. That gives ncc a chance to check permissions, bounds, alignment, width, and mode. It is safer than raw addr access because the source contract remains visible.

symbols.label: load T [address]
symbols.documentation: load copies exactly size T bytes from address into an existing place. It adds no bounds, null, alignment, lifetime or provenance checks.

symbols.label: type
symbols.documentation: Groups named structs, enums, unions and layout contracts. Split large models into focused types instead of enlarging run or stc.

symbols.label: stc
symbols.documentation: Declares the container's single mutable state section. Only one stc section is allowed; declarations without an initial <- write retain indeterminate bits.

symbols.label: in
symbols.documentation: in introduces the physical inputs of a function. Parameters use name >> Type and the result follows ->.

symbols.label: fa
symbols.documentation: Contains the explicit final material path. It lowers to the selected backend and performs no automatic cleanup or resource release.

symbols.label: const
symbols.documentation: Groups immutable compile-time values. Constants allocate no mutable state and must be materializable by the selected target.

symbols.label: local
symbols.documentation: Groups local storage separately from persistent state. Split it by responsibility when its declarations stop being easy to scan.

symbols.label: fn
symbols.documentation: Groups functions by visibility and responsibility. A function named run has no entrypoint behavior unless ref main or to main selects it.

symbols.label: public
symbols.documentation: Exposes the grouped declarations through the container's external interface.

symbols.label: internal
symbols.documentation: Shares grouped declarations inside the current package while keeping them outside the public interface.

symbols.label: private
symbols.documentation: Restricts grouped declarations to their owning container.

symbols.label: routine
symbols.documentation: routine is the basal callable surface that lowers toward machine through the closed lowering plan. It is not high-level fn. Parameters, returns, ABI hooks, spans, raw blocks, and evidence boundaries must stay visible to later seal verification.

symbols.label: raw
symbols.documentation: raw marks a block where dangerous operations are intentional: memory access, address use, width-sensitive loads, stores, shifts, and machine-lowerable primitives. The compiler must not pretend raw is safe; it records hazards and evidence boundaries.

symbols.label: verify
symbols.documentation: verify is the official basal verification surface. It may check memory, constants, routine outcomes, and evidence-driven conditions. It replaces probe as the primary spelling while keeping compatibility documented. Verification spans must be preserved for reports and seals.

symbols.label: report
symbols.documentation: report is the basal structured output surface. It declares status, emitted values, memory summaries, hashes, and table/lowering/NBB information without depending on runtime print. It is designed for evidence and seal reporting rather than casual console output.

symbols.label: program
symbols.documentation: Defines the ordinary short container. Add an explicit role only when runtime, kernel, machine or another material domain changes compilation.

symbols.label: network
symbols.documentation: Defines a network service container with explicit sockets, buffers, timing and error handling controlled by source operations.

symbols.label: tooling
symbols.documentation: Defines compiler tooling such as formatters, analyzers, package commands or language services.

symbols.label: security
symbols.documentation: Defines explicit security mechanisms and policy operations without making raw source automatically safe.

symbols.label: ai
symbols.documentation: Defines model or agent operations through explicit providers, buffers and execution contracts.

symbols.label: stack
symbols.documentation: Reserves explicit function-frame places. Exiting the block does not initialize, restore, destroy or release them.

symbols.label: abi
symbols.documentation: Defines an explicit calling convention, register, stack, aggregate and symbol contract.

symbols.label: store
symbols.documentation: Writes exactly size T bytes to an address without implicit validation.

symbols.label: copy
symbols.documentation: Copies exactly count bytes. Overlap, validity and lifetime are the programmer’s responsibility.

symbols.label: fill
symbols.documentation: Writes the low byte of value count times to destination.

symbols.label: addr
symbols.documentation: Produces the raw numeric address of a place without attaching ownership or bounds.

symbols.label: size
symbols.documentation: Produces the target layout size of Type in bytes at compile time.

symbols.label: align
symbols.documentation: Produces the target layout alignment of Type in bytes at compile time.

symbols.label: offset
symbols.documentation: Produces the byte offset of a material aggregate field at compile time.

symbols.label: static
symbols.documentation: static places initialized bytes in the binary image with explicit target layout and linkage.

symbols.label: to main
symbols.documentation: Defines an inline entry of at most 30 logical statements. Larger or deeply nested entries belong in a named function selected with ref main.

types.label: addr
types.documentation: addr is a raw address. It can identify memory but does not by itself prove type, lifetime, alignment, bounds, or ownership. Dereferencing requires conversion into a typed pointer, site, or raw block with hazards and evidence boundaries preserved.

types.label: p
types.documentation: p<T> is a typed pointer carrying element type and expected representation. It is more explicit than a C void pointer but still potentially dangerous. Nullability, provenance, aliasing, alignment, and dereference permission are separate contracts enforced by ncc.

types.label: p mut
types.documentation: p mut<T> is a mutable typed pointer. It permits writes only when the program has suitable authority and alias rules allow mutation. The IDE marks it as high risk because double mutable aliases, stale provenance, and bad alignment must be diagnosed.

types.label: ref
types.documentation: ref<T> represents a safer reference surface where nC can preserve provenance, lifetime, and alias intent. It should be preferred when raw address power is unnecessary. Unlike addr, a ref must remain tied to a valid source and type contract.

types.label: ref mut
types.documentation: ref mut<T> represents exclusive mutable reference intent. It should not silently coexist with other mutable aliases. The editor explains the model, while ncc performs the actual alias, lifetime, stale-site, and move/use diagnostics.

types.label: site
types.documentation: site<T> represents memory with known origin and contract. It gives the compiler more evidence than a raw address, including owner, region, permission, and possible bounds. Stale site references or incompatible memory contracts must be rejected, not guessed.

types.label: memRegion
types.documentation: memRegion<T> is a first-class bounded memory region. It connects pointer-like access with length, element type, provenance, and alignment expectations. This makes indexing, conversion to slices/spans, and lowering to machine load/store auditable instead of implicit.

types.label: slice
types.documentation: slice<T> is a bounded contiguous view over a region or collection. It should carry start and length information so out-of-bounds access can be diagnosed. It is a safer projection than handing raw pointer arithmetic to ordinary code.

types.label: span
types.documentation: span<T> is a bounded view that carries length and provenance into code using it. It is useful for iteration, safe indexing, and FFI contracts that expose pointer-plus-length layouts without losing the fact that the two values belong together.

types.label: int
types.detail: Baseical whole-number type in ordinary nC source.
types.documentation: int is the normal whole-number surface for high-level and runtime nC examples. It is deliberately ordinary, readable, and checked by ncc before execution. Use explicit width types when binary layout, overflow policy, machine lowering, or FFI representation must be fixed.

types.label: bool
types.documentation: bool represents true or false in nC conditions, verification expressions, routine returns, and report decisions. It is not an integer alias in the IDE dictionary: ncc owns conversions, truthiness diagnostics, and any profile-specific representation used during lowering.

types.label: str
types.documentation: str is the short official text spelling used by current nC examples. It models text as a language value rather than a raw byte pointer. Encoding, rendering, concatenation, and output rules remain explicit so strict profiles can diagnose unsafe implicit formatting.

types.label: string
types.documentation: string is documented as the readable long-form alias of str for IDE explanation and user search. The compiler line still decides accepted spelling by profile. The editor points both spellings to the same text contract and import-free type documentation.

types.label: byte
types.documentation: byte is an unsigned 8-bit value used when representation matters: buffers, bytes<N>, memory views, binary records, primitive data lanes, and machine lowering. It avoids ambiguous int width and makes overflow, endian, load, and store diagnostics easier to audit.

types.label: ft32
types.documentation: ft32 is the compact floating-point lane for real-number data that should fit four-byte storage. Use it for dense numeric arrays, vector-friendly values, and binary contracts where ft64 would waste bandwidth or change layout.

types.label: word
types.documentation: word is an unsigned 16-bit value. Use it when a field, port, protocol, or packed binary structure must be exactly two bytes wide. The IDE describes it as representation-bearing; ncc remains authority for range, endian, and lowering checks.

types.label: dword
types.documentation: dword is an unsigned 32-bit value. It is preferred over ambiguous int when basal constants, raw memory loads, binary headers, and machine-facing calculations need stable width. It carries fixed arithmetic expectations into diagnostics and NBB/lowering metadata.

types.label: qword
types.documentation: qword is an unsigned 64-bit value. It is common for addresses, counters, hashes, sizes, and machine-adjacent records where exact width matters. The editor highlights it as a fixed-width type; ncc verifies range and representation.

types.label: signed
types.documentation: signed describes values whose arithmetic keeps a sign bit and whose shifts or overflow rules may differ from unsigned forms. Use explicit sbyte, sword, sdword, or sqword when the exact signed width must survive type checking and lowering.

types.label: unsigned
types.documentation: unsigned describes width-bearing values with no sign bit. byte, word, dword, and qword are the official fixed-width unsigned forms. Prefer them for binary contracts, memory records, FFI fields, and machine lowering instead of relying on implicit integer width.

types.label: array
types.documentation: array<T, N> represents a fixed-size collection whose element type and length are part of the contract. It is suitable for deterministic layout, static loops, and bounds-aware indexing. Dynamic growth belongs to list, queue, dinArray, or memRegion surfaces.

types.label: list
types.documentation: list<T> models an ordered growable collection with one element type and runtime length. Use lista.push(x), lista.get(i), lista.set(i, x), and lista.len(). Out-of-bounds reads return the typed default; invalid writes return false.

types.label: queue
types.documentation: queue<T> models first-in-first-out collection behavior with one element type and runtime length. Use cola.push(x), cola.pop(), cola.get(i), and cola.len(). pop removes from the head; out-of-bounds reads return the typed default, keeping interactive programs alive.

types.label: vector
types.documentation: vector<T> is the growable aggregate array surface for typed indexed storage. It is useful for arrays of structs, runtime push/get/set workflows, and backend lowering as a descriptor with data pointer, length, capacity, and typed stride.

types.label: dinarray
types.documentation: dinArray<T> is the dynamic array family used for growable indexed storage when fixed arrays are too rigid. It belongs to the collection contract, not raw memory. binary and unbinary variants describe serialization direction rather than hidden pointer authority.

types.label: Result
types.documentation: Result<T, E> carries either a success value of type T or recoverable error data of type E. It keeps error handling visible in function signatures instead of hiding failure behind implicit exceptions or unchecked sentinel values.

diagnostics.label: E_PTR_NULL_DEREF_001
diagnostics.detail: Nullable pointer/ref used without explicit nullability or refinement.

diagnostics.label: E_PTR_OUT_OF_BOUNDS_001
diagnostics.detail: Pointer, span, slice or memRegion access is outside known bounds.
diagnostics.documentation: Use bounded region/slice/span access or prove the bounds.

diagnostics.label: E_PTR_ALIGNMENT_001
diagnostics.detail: Load/store/cast requires stricter alignment than the address or pointer provides.
diagnostics.documentation: Use aligned storage or explicit raw authority.

diagnostics.label: E_USE_AUTH_POLICY_REQUIRED_001
diagnostics.documentation: Use auth imports only in authorized modes with policy.

diagnostics.label: E_PTR_TYPE_002
diagnostics.documentation: The pointer operation expected one element type but observed a different runtime or declared type. Keep casts explicit, use pCast only with authority, or change the pointee type so pRead and pWrite agree with the memory cell.

diagnostics.label: E_PTR_LOWERING_001
diagnostics.detail: Pointer operation cannot lower to the selected machine target.
diagnostics.documentation: The compiler could not map a pointer load, store, offset, difference, or address materialization to the active backend profile. Check width, endian, alignment, volatile or atomic requirements, and whether the operation must live under explicit raw authority.
